env.name: PORT
env.why: The only variable this app reads. src/server.js:15 is `var port = process.env.PORT || 3000`, and that port is the whole of the app's own origin: there is no base-URL setting, no allowlist and no callback URL anywhere in src/. 3000 is set explicitly rather than left to the default so that app_url and the runbook cannot drift from what the process actually binds.

dropped.why: Linting is the static gate's job: `bsf gates static` runs the repo's own linter and compares each rule's per-file count against .factory/guardrails/baselines.json. Putting it in `build` or `test` would make a baselined lint violation fail the trial as a build error and would count the same finding twice. It is still runnable in the sandbox — `npm run lint` works once `npm ci` has run, and was run here (exit 0) — it is just not in the build path.

Replaced with `npm ci`, which installs exactly what the committed package-lock.json pins and fails loudly if the lock file and package.json disagree, so the sandbox cannot silently resolve a different dependency tree from one round to the next. `npm ci` was the command actually run and verified here; `npm install` was not.

Replaced with the equivalent `node src/server.js`. The trial stops the app by signalling the detached process group, and running node directly means there is no npm wrapper process between the signal and the server. `npm start` is kept in the runbook as the command a developer would type; the two run the same file.

dropped.what: the "Test / There are none. That is the point." section
dropped.why: True when it was written and no longer the instruction to follow. commands.test is now `npm test --if-present`, which runs the repo's own `test` script the moment one exists. The README is not updated here because setup may not keep changes to the repo; the runbook carries the current answer.

not_exercised.what: Tests on the default branch, and therefore total coverage
not_exercised.why: main as of commit 1f85fe2 still has no test files and no `test` script in package.json, so `npm test --if-present` runs nothing there and exits 0. That is a fact about the branch, not about the command: the command is set so that the gate stops being blind the moment a pull request brings a `test` script, which is what the amendment asked for and what several open pull requests do. Until such a branch merges, total coverage stays at the 0% floor in .factory/guardrails/coverage.json and diff coverage (80%) is the only coverage check with teeth.

not_exercised.what: A branch that adds test files without adding the `test` script
not_exercised.why: `npm test --if-present` delegates to the repo's own `test` script, so a pull request that adds test/*.test.js but no script to run them passes this gate having run nothing. The guard is deliberate — see the episode — and it is the price of the trial reaching `renders` on a main that has no script yet. A change that adds tests must add the runner in the same pull request; fundamentals.md and history.md both say so, and a builder that forgets will see the tests gate pass without its tests in the output tail.

not_exercised.what: Anything that has to survive a restart
not_exercised.why: The store is two module-level variables in src/db.js (`items` and `nextId`). Every restart empties the table and resets ids to 1, and nothing is written to disk. A change about durability, a schema, a migration or a move to a real database cannot be verified here; it would need a database service added by an amendment episode.

One node process holding state in its own heap: no cluster mode, no worker pool, no lock and no transaction. Two requests interleaving inside db.add or db.remove cannot be reproduced, and nothing about state shared across processes can be checked.

not_exercised.what: HTTPS, a reverse proxy, a non-localhost origin, or any deployment concern
not_exercised.why: The app listens on plain HTTP and the sandbox reaches it at 127.0.0.1:3000. The repo has no Dockerfile, compose file, devcontainer or deploy configuration, so there is nothing here that describes another origin. Secure cookie flags, `trust proxy`, CORS, HSTS and host-based routing have no environment in this sandbox to be checked against.

express is the single runtime dependency and src/ makes no outbound network call of any kind, so there is nothing to stub and no provider test mode to name. The stubs list is empty because none is needed, not because one was skipped. A change that adds an outbound call needs an amendment episode to add its stub before it can be verified.

Amendment. Read amend.json: a builder reports that commands.test is null, so `bsf gates tests` returns the neutral "this repo has no test command" verdict and never runs the tests its pull request adds. It asks for commands.test = "npm test". Checked the branch the amendment will be measured against: `git log` is at 1f85fe2 and package.json has `start` and `lint` and no `test` script, and there is no test/ directory. The pull request's own contents could not be read — the GitHub integrity policy refused pull-request content to this role — so amend.json's description of it is what this round is built on.
episode.observed: The need is real and the literal request is unsafe here. main has no `test` script, and on main `npm test` exits 1 with `Missing script: "test"`.
episode.changed: Nothing yet; went to read what the trial does with a failing test step before choosing the command.

episode.tried: Read the trial itself rather than guessing: .github/workflows/factory-setup-trial.yml, and trialSandbox/reachedTier inside the vendored runner.
episode.observed: Three facts decide this. (1) factory-setup is a workflow_dispatch and the trial job checks out the dispatched ref with no override, so the commands are measured against main as it is today — no `test` script. (2) reachedTier returns "static" outright if the test step fails, and the run and screenshot steps are skipped entirely unless every earlier step passed, so a test command that fails on main does not merely lose the test step, it collapses the claim from renders to static for every round. (3) After build and test pass, the trial re-runs them in an empty temporary directory and records a "control" step that fails if they pass there too — so the command must also fail outside this repo.
episode.changed: Rejected the literal `npm test`. The command has to satisfy all three at once: run the repo's tests where a `test` script exists, exit 0 on a main that has none, and fail in an empty directory.

episode.tried: Measured the candidates in the trial's own closed environment (`env -i` with PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG, CI, PORT) under node v24.22.3 and npm 11.19.1, in three places: this repo at main, an empty directory, and a scratch copy of the repo carrying the shape amend.json describes.
episode.observed: `npm test` — main: exit 1, `Missing script: "test"`. Empty directory: exit 254 (no package.json). Collapses the tier. `node --test` (bare) — empty directory: exit 0, "tests 0", so the control step would fail it and the tier would be static for the opposite reason. `npm test --if-present` — main: exit 0, runs nothing; empty directory: exit 254; scratch copy with a `test` script: runs the tests.
episode.changed: Set commands.test to `npm test --if-present`. It is the repo's own `npm test`, guarded only against the window in which main has no script yet; the guard is on the script, and in an empty directory npm fails on the missing package.json before the guard is reached, so the control step still proves the command depends on this repo.
